_note: Readings this archive has WITHDRAWN, and must not state as fact again.
A retired phrase is this archive's own wording and never a document's, which is
what makes it checkable where a general prose gate cannot be: nobody quotes a
source saying «a blank of twenty-four years». If the string is on a page, this
archive put it there.
WHERE THEY ARE ALLOWED, and why this list needs the exception more than the rule:
on /corrections, which exists to quote them; and in DATED LOGS — the work list,
the searched register, the change log — which record what was believed on a day
and MUST NOT be edited when the belief changes. Rewriting a log to match a later
finding is the failure this archive's whole method is against.
TWO ENTRIES WERE REMOVED ON THE FIRST RUN, and why matters more than the tool.
«No record has been found for them» is not a withdrawn WORDING. It is a
sentence that is false about thirty people and true about four hundred — the
fix on 17 September made grade.js say it only when a person genuinely has no
record, and it says it correctly on every page this gate flagged. And «may
never have existed» reached ten person pages only inside MENTION SNIPPETS,
which quote /open-questions and /corrections reporting the error.
So the rule for this list: a phrase belongs here only if it is a PROPOSITION
this archive has withdrawn in every context — never a sentence that is
sometimes true, and never one the archive's own reporting quotes.
